turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Mr Ellison, I'll just pop these obs in before the doctor gets going. Pulse ninety-eight, blood pressure one-eighteen over seventy-six, temperature thirty-seven point two, oxygen sats ninety-eight percent. Lips look a bit dry.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Yep, sorry, this screen's playing up. What was the pulse again?
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Ninety-eight. I'll let you get on. His wife's come in with him.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Right. So what's the problem today?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Nothing much. Bit of a gut thing after a wedding. I'm fine, honestly.
[SEG0006] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's not fine. He's been running to the loo since Sunday night, and he spewed in the carpark just now.
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Once. I chucked once. The diarrhoea's already settling, it's not a big deal.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Hang on, the screen's frozen again. Wedding, when was that?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Saturday arvo. Cousin's wedding in Newcastle, traffic was a shocker on the way up. I had the prawns off the buffet, that's all.
[SEG0010] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Aunty Marg and two of the cousins are crook with the same thing. They messaged this morning.
[SEG0011] person_2 (DOCTOR): How many bowel motions are we talking?
[SEG0012] person_3 (PATIENT): I didn't count properly, a handful, six maybe eight, watery. Who's counting.
[SEG0013] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any blood in it, or black stool?
[SEG0014] person_3 (PATIENT): Nah. No blood. Just water, basically.
[SEG0015] person_2 (DOCTOR): And the vomiting, sorry, say again how many times?
[SEG0016] person_3 (PATIENT): Once, this morning, in the carpark. Yesterday I dry-retched a bit. I wouldn't call that vomiting.
[SEG0017] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He vomited three times yesterday, I watched him. And he goes dizzy when he stands up.
[SEG0018] person_3 (PATIENT): I'm not dizzy. I stood up quick. Don't turn it into a drama.
[SEG0019] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever at home? Pain in the tummy?
[SEG0020] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever. There's some cramping low down, comes and goes. Nothing dramatic.
[SEG0021] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He's hardly drunk a thing. A few sips of water since last night, and he keeps waving the glass away.
[SEG0022] person_3 (PATIENT): I've had sips. I'm not dehydrated.
[SEG0023] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sorry, fluids, can you repeat that? I was clicking the wrong tab.
[SEG0024] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): A few sips of water since last night. And he's been taking Imodium.
[SEG0025] person_2 (DOCTOR): Loperamide. What dose?
[SEG0026] person_3 (PATIENT): Two milligram tablets from the chemist. Two last night, two this morning. They work. I don't see the issue.
[SEG0027] person_2 (DOCTOR): With a gastro bug like this I'd rather you stopped them. Let it out, especially with other people from the same meal crook.
[SEG0028] person_3 (PATIENT): Yeah, alright, if you reckon. I only took them 'cause the cramps were annoying.
[SEG0029] person_2 (DOCTOR): Anything else you take? Regular meds?

[SEG0030] person_3 (PATIENT): Pantoprazole, forty milligrams, but I stopped it in March. Heartburn's been fine since. And there was azithromycin from a Bali trip years back, never opened the pack, so that doesn't count. The GP also left ondansetron and I never took that either.
[SEG0031] person_4 (FAMILY_MEMBER): You did. Sunday, you took one of those wafers by mouth. Said your head went fuzzy, so you didn't take another.
[SEG0032] person_3 (PATIENT): Oh, right. One four milligram wafer, then I stopped. Binned the rest. Fuzzy head's gone.
[SEG0033] person_2 (DOCTOR): Let me just read that back. Pantoprazole stopped in March, and a single four milligram ondansetron wafer you didn't continue?
[SEG0034] person_3 (PATIENT): Yep. No allergies, by the way, before you go looking.
[SEG0035] person_2 (DOCTOR): Okay. Hop up on the bed, I'll feel your tummy. Sorry, one sec, this login's timed out again.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Abdomen's soft, tender low on the left, no guarding. Lips are cracked and the mouth's dry. Chest is clear, heart sounds are normal.
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Told you. Can we wrap this up? I've got a shift at the warehouse tomorrow.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Looks like foodborne gastro from that wedding meal. That's my working impression, not nailed down. And you're mildly dehydrated, nothing wild.

[SEG0039] person_2 (DOCTOR): Sip Hydralyte, little and often, not big gulps of plain water. Leave the loperamide alone. If you're still opening your bowels more than a few times by Friday, or you can't keep fluid down, then we'll send a stool culture. I'm not ordering it today.
[SEG0040] person_3 (PATIENT): Friday's miles off. I'll be sweet.

[SEG0041] person_2 (DOCTOR): If it's not settling by Friday, come back and see me. Sooner if there's blood, bad pain, you stop weeing, or you feel faint, go to emergency. Your wife can nag you about the drinks.
